3.1.1.tools: axe-core `html-has-lang`, `html-lang-valid` and `html-xml-lang-mismatch` decide presence and validity of the page language; the static scanner flags `<html>` without `lang` in templates and layout components. A human only confirms the declared language matches the main content.
procedure: Inspect the root `<html>` element (or the document language setting for PDF/Office).
Confirm a `lang` attribute exists with a valid BCP 47 tag.
Compare the tag with the predominant language of the content; a valid but wrong tag still fails.
Repeat for each template, SPA route shell and iframe document in scope.
patterns: `<html>` with no `lang` attribute (common in hand-written templates and some SSR shells).
Invalid or empty values such as `lang=""`, `lang="english"` or `lang="en_US"`.
Framework default left in place, e.g. `lang="en"` on a site whose content is German.
`lang` and `xml:lang` that disagree on XHTML documents.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
  <head><title>Accueil</title></head>

3.1.2.applies: language, inline passages, quotations, multilingual content, language switchers
3.1.2.tools: axe-core `valid-lang` only checks that `lang` values on descendants are valid; it cannot find untagged foreign passages. A static scanner can flag language-switcher links (e.g. text `Deutsch`, `Español`) without `lang`; a human must identify passages in another language.
procedure: Read the page and list passages, quotes, names of languages and UI labels written in a language other than the page default.
Check each passage (or its nearest container) carries a correct `lang` attribute.
Ignore proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language and words that have become part of the surrounding language.
Verify any `lang` values used are valid BCP 47 tags.
patterns: Language-picker links like `Deutsch` without `lang="de"`.
Block quotes or testimonials in another language without `lang` on the `<blockquote>`.
React i18n components rendering fallback strings in the default language inside a translated page without marking them.
Invalid values such as `lang="sp"`.

3.1.3.applies: text content, jargon, idioms, technical terms
3.1.3.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A static scanner can list `<abbr>`, `<dfn>` and glossary links as evidence of a mechanism; identifying unusual words is human judgement.
procedure: Identify idioms, jargon and words used in an unusual or restricted way.
For each, check a mechanism gives the specific definition: inline definition, `<dfn>`, link to a glossary, or a definition list.
Confirm the mechanism is reachable from each use (or the glossary is linked consistently).
patterns: Domain jargon (e.g. "amortize", "idempotent") with no definition or glossary link.
Idioms such as "ballpark figure" left unexplained.
A glossary page exists but is not linked from the terms that need it.

pass.code: Each request is idempotent.

3.1.4.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A static scanner can find all-caps tokens and `<abbr>` elements lacking an expansion; a human decides which are abbreviations needing expansion.
procedure: List abbreviations, acronyms and initialisms on the page.
Check each is expanded on first use, via `<abbr title>` plus visible expansion, a glossary link, or a consistent definition mechanism.
Confirm the expansion is available to all users (not only a mouse-hover `title`).
patterns: Acronyms such as `SLA` or `WCAG` used with no expansion anywhere.
Expansion only in a `title` tooltip that keyboard and touch users cannot reach.
Same abbreviation with different meanings on one page and no disambiguation.

pass.code: We meet our SLA (service level agreement) for all plans.

3.1.5.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A readability formula (e.g. Flesch-Kincaid) run by the page runner or a script gives an estimate; a human confirms whether a supplemental version or simpler text is needed.
procedure: Excluding proper names and titles, estimate the reading level of the main text.
If it needs more than lower secondary education, check for supplemental content (summary, illustrations, audio) or a simpler version.
Confirm the supplement conveys the key information.
patterns: Dense legal or academic prose with no plain-language summary.
Long sentences with nested clauses and passive voice in task instructions.

3.1.6.applies: text content, heteronyms, languages with ambiguous pronunciation
3.1.6.tools: No axe-core rule applies. Detecting words whose meaning depends on pronunciation is human judgement; a scanner can only check that `<ruby>` markup is well formed.
procedure: Find words whose meaning is ambiguous without knowing the pronunciation (heteronyms, kanji readings, unvowelled Hebrew/Arabic).
Check a mechanism gives the pronunciation: inline, `<ruby>`, glossary or audio.
patterns: Heteronyms such as "read" or "lead" in contexts where both meanings fit and no clarification is given.
Japanese names with non-standard readings and no furigana.

3.2.1.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A static scanner can flag `onFocus`/`focus` handlers that call `submit()`, change `location`, open windows or move focus; a page runner can tab through every focusable element and detect URL changes, new windows or focus jumps. A human confirms whether a change is a change of context.
procedure: Tab (and Shift+Tab) through every focusable component without activating anything.
Watch for new windows, navigation, form submission, large content rearrangement or focus being moved elsewhere.
Repeat with a screen reader's virtual cursor for elements that receive focus programmatically.
Record each component whose focus alone causes a change of context.
patterns: `<select onfocus="this.form.submit()">` or a React `onFocus` that calls `navigate()`.
Focusing a field opens a modal or pop-up window automatically.
`onFocus={() => nextRef.current.focus()}` that throws focus away from the element.

3.2.2.applies: forms, select menus, radio buttons, checkboxes, custom widgets
3.2.2.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A static scanner can flag `onchange`/`onChange`/`input` handlers that submit forms, navigate or move focus; a page runner can change each control value and detect navigation or focus jumps. A human confirms whether users were advised beforehand.
procedure: Change the setting of every input (type, select an option, toggle a checkbox or radio) without pressing a submit button.
Note any navigation, form submission, new window or unexpected focus move.
For each change of context found, check whether instructions before the component warn about the behaviour.
Check keyboard selection in `<select>` does not trigger navigation on each arrow key.
patterns: `<select onchange="location=this.value">` jump menus without a Go button.
React `onChange={e => router.push(e.target.value)}` on a dropdown.
Checkbox that auto-submits the form (`onChange={() => form.submit()}`).
Filling the last digit of a code field auto-submits and navigates without warning.

3.2.3.applies: navigation, headers, footers, menus, skip links, sets of pages
3.2.3.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A page runner can crawl several pages and compare the order of landmark and navigation link lists; a human confirms differences are not user-initiated.
procedure: Pick a representative set of pages that share navigation (header, sidebar, footer, breadcrumbs, search).
Compare the relative order of repeated navigation items across the pages.
Accept added or removed items as long as the remaining items keep the same relative order.
Exclude changes the user initiated (e.g. personalising a menu).
patterns: Main menu items reordered on different page templates (e.g. marketing vs. account layouts).
Search box before navigation on some pages and after it on others.
React layout variants that render nav links from different, unsorted arrays.

3.2.4.applies: icons, buttons, links, components repeated across pages
3.2.4.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A page runner can collect accessible names of components with the same function (same `href`, same icon, same handler) across pages and flag inconsistent names; a human confirms same functionality.
procedure: Identify components with the same function across the set of pages (search, print, download, home icon, cart).
Compare their visible labels, accessible names and text alternatives.
Flag components with the same function but different identification.
patterns: Search button labelled "Search" on one page and "Find" on another.
The same download icon with `alt="Download"` in one place and `alt="Save file"` elsewhere.
Shared React component used with different `aria-label` props for the same action.

3.2.5.applies: navigation, pop-ups, new windows, automatic updates, redirects, forms
3.2.5.tools: axe-core `meta-refresh-no-exceptions` flags `<meta http-equiv=refresh>` with a delay; a static scanner can flag `target="_blank"` without a warning, `window.open` on load, and `setInterval` reloads; a human confirms that changes happen only on user request or can be turned off.
procedure: Load each page and wait: note any automatic redirect, refresh or content replacement.
Check links and buttons that open new windows warn the user beforehand.
Check any automatic update has a mechanism to turn it off.
Verify redirects are done server-side instead of timed client redirects.
patterns: `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5; url=/new">`.
`target="_blank"` links with no text or icon indicating a new window.
`window.open()` fired on page load or on focus.
Carousel or feed that replaces content automatically with no way to stop it.

pass.code: Terms (opens in new window)

3.2.6.applies: help, contact details, chat, FAQ links, sets of pages
3.2.6.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A page runner can crawl a set of pages and record the DOM order position of help mechanisms (contact links, `mailto:`/`tel:` links, chat widget, FAQ link) relative to other content; a human confirms they appear in the same relative order and identifies which help mechanisms exist.
procedure: Identify the help mechanisms offered (human contact details, contact mechanism, self-help option, automated contact such as a chatbot).
Open several pages in the set that contain them (same page variation / breakpoint).
Check each mechanism appears in the same order relative to other page content on every page.
Remember the SC does not require help to be provided; it requires consistency where it is repeated.
patterns: Contact link in the header on some pages and moved to the footer on others.
Chat widget injected only on some templates, or before main content on some and after it on others.
Checkout templates that drop the help link used everywhere else, then re-add it in a different position.

3.3.1.applies: forms, error messages, validation, required fields
3.3.1.tools: No axe-core rule directly tests error messages. A static scanner can flag inputs with `aria-invalid` but no `aria-describedby`/`aria-errormessage`, and error messages styled only by colour; a page runner can submit forms with empty/invalid data and dump the accessibility tree for errors. A human confirms the error text identifies the item and describes the problem.
procedure: Submit each form empty and with invalid data.
Check each detected error identifies the item in error and describes the problem in text.
Check the error is programmatically associated (`aria-describedby`/`aria-errormessage`, `aria-invalid`) or announced.
Confirm errors are not conveyed only by colour, border or icon.
patterns: Field turns red with no text message.
Generic "There was an error" banner not naming the field.
Error text placed near the field but not associated, e.g. `<span class="error">` without `aria-describedby`.
Client validation prevents submission silently.

pass.code: Email: enter an address like name@example.com.

3.3.2.applies: forms, inputs, required fields, format hints, custom widgets
3.3.2.tools: axe-core `form-field-multiple-labels` catches one labelling problem; `label` (tagged 4.1.2) finds unlabelled inputs. A static scanner can flag inputs relying only on `placeholder`; a human confirms the visible labels/instructions are sufficient (required fields, formats).
procedure: Find every input that needs user entry.
Check each has a visible label or instructions when the content requires input.
Check required fields and expected formats (dates, passwords) are indicated before submission.
Check grouped controls (radio sets, date parts) have a group label (e.g. `<fieldset>`/`<legend>`).
patterns: `placeholder` used as the only label and disappearing on input.
Required fields marked only with colour or an unexplained asterisk.
Date field with no indication of the expected format.
Radio buttons with no question/legend.

3.3.3.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A page runner can submit invalid values and capture the resulting messages; a human judges whether suggestions are given where known and safe.
procedure: Enter invalid values for each field with a known correct format or range.
Check the error message suggests how to correct it (format, allowed values, closest match).
Accept omission only where a suggestion would jeopardise security or the purpose (e.g. a password).
patterns: "Invalid input" without saying what is expected.
Date rejected without stating the format.
Unrecognised city not followed by likely matches.

3.3.4.applies: forms, checkout, legal commitments, financial transactions, data deletion, test submissions
3.3.4.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A static scanner can find destructive or payment forms; a human must walk the flow to confirm submissions are reversible, checked, or confirmed.
procedure: Identify pages that cause legal commitments, financial transactions, modification/deletion of user data, or submit test responses.
Complete each flow and check at least one of: reversible, data checked with a chance to correct, or a review/confirm step.
Verify the confirm/review step really lets users correct information before final submission.
patterns: One-click "Delete account" with no confirmation or undo.
Payment submitted directly from the card form with no review page.
Exam answers submitted immediately on selection.

3.3.7.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A static scanner can spot duplicated fields (same `name`/`autocomplete` token across steps) as candidates; a human walks the process to confirm previously entered data is auto-populated or selectable.

List information the user is asked for more than once.
Check repeated information is auto-populated or available to select (e.g. "same as billing address").
Accept exceptions: re-entry essential (memory game), needed for security (password confirmation), or the earlier data is no longer valid.

3.3.8.applies: authentication, login, password fields, CAPTCHA, one-time codes
3.3.8.tools: No axe-core rule applies. A static scanner can flag `onpaste` / `onPaste` handlers that `preventDefault`, `autocomplete="off"` on username/password fields, and split one-time-code inputs; a page runner can test paste and password-manager autofill. A human confirms whether any cognitive function test is used without an alternative, mechanism, or allowed exception (object/personal content recognition).
procedure: Walk every login, sign-up, step-up and password-reset step.
Identify any cognitive function test (remember a password, transcribe a code, solve a puzzle).
Check an alternative method exists or a mechanism assists (paste allowed, password manager autofill, copy-paste of codes, email link, passkey).
Accept object recognition or recognising user-supplied personal content (AA only).
Check CAPTCHA types used and that a non-cognitive alternative is available.
patterns: Password field that blocks paste: `onPaste={e => e.preventDefault()}`.
`autocomplete="off"` or non-standard field names that stop password managers.
OTP split into 6 inputs that break paste.
Text-transcription CAPTCHA with no alternative.

Any 3.3.8 failure pattern.

4.1.1.tools: axe-core `duplicate-id` and `duplicate-id-active` are tagged deprecated and should not produce 4.1.1 failures; under WCAG 2.2 parsing is not a requirement and is always satisfied. Duplicate IDs that are referenced by `for`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby` or `aria-controls` are still real defects, reported against 1.3.1 or 4.1.2 (axe `duplicate-id-aria`).
procedure: Do not report failures of 4.1.1 in a WCAG 2.2 audit; mark it as not applicable/satisfied.
Route markup problems that affect users to the SC they break: broken label/ARIA references to 1.3.1 or 4.1.2, invalid roles/nesting to 4.1.2.
patterns: Duplicate `id` referenced by `<label for>` so the wrong input is labelled (report under 1.3.1/4.1.2).
Duplicate `id` targeted by `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` giving the wrong accessible name or description (report under 4.1.2).
Unclosed or misnested elements that change the accessibility tree (report under the affected SC, usually 1.3.1).

4.1.2.applies: custom widgets, forms, links, buttons, iframes, ARIA, dynamic states
4.1.2.tools: axe-core covers many objective failures: `button-name`, `link-name`, `input-button-name`, `label`, `select-name`, `aria-*` validity rules (`aria-allowed-attr`, `aria-required-attr`, `aria-valid-attr-value`, `aria-roles`, `aria-hidden-focus`), `nested-interactive`, `frame-title`, `summary-name` and more. A static scanner can flag clickable `div`/`span` with handlers but no role/tabindex; a page runner can dump the accessibility tree and toggle widgets to check `aria-expanded`/`aria-checked`/`aria-selected` updates. A human with a screen reader confirms names are meaningful and states are announced.
procedure: Run axe-core and fix objective name/role/ARIA errors.
List every interactive component, especially custom widgets built from `div`/`span`.
Inspect the accessibility tree: each has a correct role, a name, and exposed states/values (expanded, checked, selected, pressed, current value).
Operate each widget and confirm state changes update in the tree and are announced by a screen reader.
Check user-settable values (sliders, custom selects) can be set by assistive technology.
patterns:
`
Menu
` with no role, tabindex or keyboard handler.
Icon-only button `<button><svg/></button>` with no accessible name.
Disclosure toggle without `aria-expanded`, or with a value that never updates.
Custom checkbox styled `<span class="checked">` with no `role="checkbox"`/`aria-checked`.
`aria-hidden="true"` on a container that holds focusable elements.

4.1.3.applies: status messages, live regions, toasts, search results counts, form submission feedback, loading states
4.1.3.tools: No axe-core rule directly checks status messages (it only validates ARIA used on them). A static scanner can flag toast/alert/notification components rendered without `role="status"`, `role="alert"` or `aria-live`; a page runner can trigger actions and observe live-region content changes. A human with a screen reader confirms messages are announced without receiving focus.
procedure: Identify status messages: results counts, success/confirmation messages, progress, errors after actions, cart updates.
Trigger each one and confirm it does not move focus.
Check the message container has an appropriate role or live property (`status`, `alert`, `log`, `progressbar`, `aria-live`) present before the content changes.
Verify with a screen reader that the message is announced.
patterns: Toast appended to the DOM with no `role`/`aria-live`.
Live region created at the same time as its message, so it is not announced.
"12 results found" text updated silently after filtering.
Using `role="alert"` for every minor update, causing noisy interruptions (advisory).
